# Catalog of resolved examples

*Generated by `tests/catalog/make_catalog_md.py` from the tables in `tests/catalog/`; do not edit by hand.*

Each entry has its input, the expected result and an evidence class (below).  The same tables drive the test runners, so every row marked `ci` below is re-checked by `sh tests/run_ci.sh`, and every row can be re-checked with `sh tests/run_all.sh`.

## How to read the evidence column

| code | meaning |
|---|---|
| **L** | the expected value agrees with a classical value stored with the sample (dual graph of a rational double point; genus and self-intersection of a simple elliptic singularity; Hirzebruch-Jung continued fraction). The classical statements are quoted from standard theory, they were not re-derived here, and for characteristic p they are what the computation is compared against, not an independent proof. |
| **X** | agreement of two routes inside this repository: the prediction from the stabiliser strata (`qhPredict`) and the explicit toric resolution of the weighted blow-up (`toricResolve`). |
| **V** | an independent certificate exists in `data/certificates/` (exact test that the toric map is proper, unit-ideal identities re-expanded by `scripts/verify_cofactors.py`, exact rational test of projectivity by `scripts/projectivity_exact.py`). |
| **O** | output of the implementation only; no independent value is known to the author. |
| **N** | negative example: hypothesis (A4) fails.  The runner re-computes this with a plain Jacobian computation. |

"Confirmed" in this catalog means exactly the codes L, X or V, never O.  No row of the recorded run has a verdict MISMATCH, TORIC-FAIL, PREDICT-FAIL or CRASH (`results/summary.tsv`, 440 rows: 361 CONFIRM, 79 SKIP).

## How to run

| what | command | time |
|---|---|---|
| fast set (all `ci` rows, all unit tests, the package check) | `sh tests/run_ci.sh` | about 5 minutes |
| everything in the tables, including the heavy rows | `sh tests/run_all.sh` | about 40 minutes |
| one hypersurface | `ONLY=E8_p2 M2 --script tests/catalog/run_hypersurfaces.m2` | seconds |
| the 16 readings of Bergh's step A2 on the hard cone | `CASES=rank3 sh scripts/sweep_a2.sh` | up to an hour |

Times were measured on one laptop (Macaulay2 1.26.06) and are only a guide.

## Cyclic quotient surface singularities

Input: the cone spanned by (0,1) and (r,-q) in Z^2, that is the singularity 1/r(1,q), with trivial labels.  Expected: after Bergh's Algorithm B the fan is smooth and, after contracting (-1)-curves, the chain of exceptional curves has self-intersections -b_1, ..., -b_k where r/q = [b_1, ..., b_k] is the Hirzebruch-Jung continued fraction (evidence **L**: classical; the table was computed independently in Python with exact integers by `tests/catalog/gen_cyclic.py`, and re-evaluated to r/q by `check_catalog.py`).  Command: `M2 --script tests/catalog/run_cyclic.m2` (rows with r <= 12, about 15 s) or `TIER=all M2 --script tests/catalog/run_cyclic.m2` (r <= 16, about 1 minute).

Notation of the chain: `{3, 2}` means two curves of self-intersection -3 and -2.  Special cases: 1/r(1,1) is the cone over the rational normal curve of degree r (one curve, self-intersection -r); 1/r(1,r-1) is the A_{r-1} singularity (r-1 curves of self-intersection -2).

## Higher-dimensional simplicial cones

Input: a stacky fan given by one simplicial cone (rays, labels).  Expected: multiplicity of the cone before; number of rays and of maximal cones of the smooth output.  The runner also checks, with exact integer arithmetic independent of the package, that every maximal cone of the output has determinant +-1, that every output ray lies in the original cone, and that the original rays are kept.  Evidence **L** (single blow-up of 1/2(1,...,1), classical) or **O** (counts are regression values).  Command: `M2 --script tests/catalog/run_fans.m2`, about 5 s; heavy rows with `TIER=all`.

## The choices left open in step A2

Bergh's step A2 does not fix four things (see the Caveat in `package/ToricDestackification.m2`).  The research code `src/StackyFan.m2` exposes them as switches (`psiOrder`, `a2Extreme`, `a2Key`, `a2Interior`) and `scripts/sweep_a2.sh` runs all 2^4 = 16 readings.  Termination and correctness do not depend on the reading; the cost does.

| case | readings that finished | detail | evidence | time limit | source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1/r(1,q), r <= 6 (surfaces) | 16 of 16 | every reading gives a smooth fan and, after contracting (-1)-curves, the Hirzebruch-Jung chain | L | none | tests/catalog/run_switches.m2 (about 10 s) |
| cone e1,e2,(1,1,3) (rank 3, multiplicity 3) | 16 of 16 | every reading gives 6 rays and 7 maximal cones | O | none | tests/catalog/run_switches.m2 |
| cone e1,e2,(1,2,5) (rank 3, multiplicity 5) | 3 of 16 within 200 s | finished: last/max/nd-mult/true (85 rays, 10 s), last/max/nd-mult/false (83 rays, 9 s), last/max/mult-nd/false (145 rays, 30 s); the other 13 readings, among them all 8 with psiOrder=first and all 8 with a2Extreme=min, were cut off at 200 s.  The readings are written psiOrder/a2Extreme/a2Key/a2Interior.  Different readings give different (all smooth) fans, so the number of rays depends on the reading | O | 200 s per reading | CASES=rank3 sh scripts/sweep_a2.sh, run on 2026-10-07 (macOS laptop, one process per reading, other jobs running at the same time) |

## Hypersurfaces

Category names: S1-S4 are surfaces (3 variables), H3-H5 are higher-dimensional hypersurfaces (4 variables = threefolds, 5 = fourfolds, 6-7 = dimensions 5 and 6).

Input: a polynomial f in F_p[x,y,z,u,v,s,t] (first n variables), weights w with f quasi-homogeneous of the given degree, X = Spec F_p[x]/(f), assumed smooth away from the vertex (A4).  Expected: the verdict of `qhVerify` (CONFIRM = prediction and explicit resolution agree; SKIP = A4 fails), the orders r of the stabiliser strata, and for surfaces the resolution graph.  Columns: *features* lists p|w_i, p|d, p|r (p divides the order of a stabiliser: the quotient stack is not Deligne-Mumford) and "alt weights"; *result* is `curves, arms, centre self-intersection, genus`; *s* is the time recorded when the corpus was run.  Rows with tier `ci` are run by `tests/catalog/run_hypersurfaces.m2`; the others by `TIER=all` or `ONLY=<id>`.

### H4 fourfolds
